task.description:
WF-03 Step 4c (full test run) for ISS-0119. THIS STEP DECIDES WHETHER STEP FINAL MAY MERGE, so the standard is higher than 'run the suite and report'.

THE SITUATION, stated plainly so you are not misled by any earlier claim in this run's handoffs. `mix letflow.check` is RED on this branch and has been red on main for pre-existing reasons in the ISS-0109/ISS-0116 tenant-schema failure class (ISS-0109 is status `instrumented` -- diagnosed, NOT fixed -- with successor ISS-0116 open). REVIEWER established at Step 3d that this branch added no failure main lacks, using the argument that the branch changed ZERO compiled code so no causal path to any test outcome existed. THAT PROOF HAS EXPIRED: Step 4 added test/support/status_history.ex and test/docs/requirement_status_invariants_test.exs, so the branch is no longer a zero-code change. REVIEWER said explicitly that you must re-establish the baseline on your own evidence and may NOT inherit that finding. Do not restate it.

YOUR CENTRAL QUESTION, and the only one that gates the merge: DOES THIS BRANCH ADD ANY FAILURE THAT MAIN DOES NOT ALREADY HAVE? Answer it with evidence you generate. The honest way is a direct comparison, and you have a worked precedent for how to do it safely: §7.1 of `lib/letflow/design/iss-0119-status-file-readability.md` used a throwaway `git worktree` for exactly this, and TEST-DESIGNER performed it successfully. Use a throwaway worktree for the main-side run -- NEVER a `git checkout` in this checkout, which holds local `main` and has a live sibling worktree at letflow-wt2 on another branch. Remove the worktree afterwards and confirm it is gone.

BE AWARE OF A REAL CONFOUND before you attribute anything. ELIXIR-DEV found at Step 3 that this workspace's Postgres carries orphaned rows in `public.iss060_tenant_schemas_guard_backup` whose parent `tenants` rows are gone, and that deleting them cut one test file from 12 failures to 3; it also found Postgres at `max_connections` saturation after 11h uptime. So the failure COUNT here is partly a function of accumulated local database state and connection pressure, not only of code -- which means a raw count difference between two runs is weak evidence on its own, and two runs at different times can differ for reasons neither branch caused. Prefer comparing the SET of failing test identities (module + test name) over comparing counts, and say which failures are stable across runs versus which move. If you clean database state to get a meaningful comparison, do it for BOTH sides or neither, and say what you did.

OBSERVED COUNTS SO FAR IN THIS RUN, offered as orientation and NOT as your baseline -- you must generate your own: 15 failures at Step 3 (pre-test-files), 13 at Step 4f (9 Letflow.IdentityMigrationTest, 2 Mix.Tasks.Letflow.Check.TestTest, 1 the then-unamended A4). The A4 failure is expected to be GONE now -- TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR ran the invariant file at Step 4b and got 13 passed, 0 failures. Confirm that holds in a full-suite context too, since a file that passes alone can fail under concurrency.

WHAT TO PRODUCE:
  1. A full `mix letflow.check` run on this branch. Quote the real result verbatim -- the counts, the task's exit line, and the enumerated failures by module and test name.
  2. A full run on main, from a throwaway worktree, under conditions as close to identical as you can make them. Quote the same.
  3. A SET COMPARISON: failures present on both (pre-existing, not this branch's), failures present ONLY on the branch (these are the merge blockers), failures present only on main (interesting, report but do not act).
  4. A verdict on the central question, with the evidence that supports it. If the answer is 'the branch adds nothing', say so and show the sets. If the branch DOES add a failure, say so plainly -- that is a merge blocker and it is far better found here than after merge.
  5. Confirm the 13 invariant assertions (A0-A8 incl. A4a/A4b, A3b, and the two negative controls) pass in the full-suite context.
  6. A structured report at `test/reports/report-20260821-WF03-ISS0119-20260821.yaml`, YAML, matching the schema of the existing `test/reports/report-20260821-WF03-ISS0109-20260821.yaml` -- read that file first and follow its established shape rather than inventing one. Include the per-failure attribution and the set comparison.

RULES. Never call a red pipeline OK without a source (core-directives.md) -- attributing a failure to the ISS-0109 class requires you to show the failure MATCHES that class, not merely that the class exists. 'Probably flaky' is not an attribution without evidence. Do not fix any failing test, do not edit any test or source file, and do not touch anything under docs/status/. If you discover a NEW defect, report it to ORCH in result.issues rather than filing it yourself or fixing it.

handoffs/orchestrator.log has uncommitted ORCH edits and docs/issues/ISS-0193.yaml is a new untracked ORCH file -- leave BOTH alone, do not commit them. Stage by explicit path, never `git add -A`.
acceptance_criteria: A full mix letflow.check run on the branch was performed and its real output quoted, including enumerated failures by module and test name
A full run on main was performed from a throwaway git worktree (never a checkout in this checkout) and its real output quoted
A set comparison of failing test identities is given: both-sides, branch-only, main-only
A verdict on whether this branch adds any failure main does not already have, supported by the generated evidence and not by REVIEWER's expired proof
Any attribution to the ISS-0109/ISS-0116 class shows the failure matches that class rather than asserting it
The 13 invariant assertions are confirmed passing in full-suite context, not only in isolation
Database-state or connection-pressure interventions, if any, were applied to both sides or neither, and are described
A structured YAML report exists at test/reports/report-20260821-WF03-ISS0119-20260821.yaml following the schema of the ISS-0109 report
The throwaway worktree was removed and its removal confirmed
No test or source file was modified, nothing under docs/status/ was touched, and orchestrator.log/ISS-0193.yaml were not committed

result.summary: VERDICT: this branch adds NO failure that main does not already have. Step Final is NOT blocked by this step. IMPORTANT ON BASIS: this step ran no suite -- the user directed it to finish from the prior stopped attempt's surviving logs. One briefing premise was wrong and is corrected: tmp-testrunner/main2.log is NOT incomplete. It carries START 08:32:41Z, 'Finished in 530.2 seconds', 'Result: 1261/1274 passed (5/5 properties, 1256/1269 tests)', 'Failed: 13 tests', LETFLOW_CHECK_EXIT=1 and END 08:41:34Z. It was recovered, so the comparison is 2 branch runs vs 2 MAIN runs, not 2-vs-1, and the asymmetry limit the briefing anticipated does not apply. RAW RESULTS: branch1 1274/1287, 13 failed; branch2 1273/1287, 14 failed; main1 1259/1274, 15 failed; main2 1261/1274, 13 failed. All exit 1. COUNT DELTA CONFIRMED, NOT ASSUMED: 1282-1269 = 13 tests, properties 5/5 on both sides; git diff be74d62..HEAD adds exactly one test module (test/docs/requirement_status_invariants_test.exs) declaring exactly 13 tests. The delta IS the invariant file. SET COMPARISON by module+test name. BOTH SIDES, all 4 runs (12): 10 Letflow.IdentityMigrationTest (guard-backup ISS-0048/0050/0060 class, the same ten names in every run) + 2 Mix.Tasks.Letflow.Check.TestTest (ISS-0107 60s ExUnit.TimeoutError). BOTH SIDES, 3 of 4 runs (1): a third Check.TestTest timeout -- present on main TWICE and the branch ONCE, i.e. the branch ran FEWER, the opposite direction from a merge concern. BRANCH-ONLY (2, each a single non-reproducing observation): B1 Letflow.Identity.RoleRegistryTest 'list_roles/0 ... returns [] against an empty tenant_role table' (branch1 only); B2 Letflow.Definitions.PromotionAssertionRerunTest 'AC2 -- sandbox receives only artifact fixtures' (branch2 only). MAIN-ONLY (2, both in main1 only): M1 Letflow.EngineTest 'create/2 (REQ-059 AC6) child pin inheritance'; M2 Letflow.Engine.ReconstructionTest 'AC6 -- {:lock_contention, instance_id}'. ATTRIBUTION, shown rather than asserted. B2 is a FOUR-AXIS match to ISS-0109's OWN enumerated failure 14: same module ISS-0109 is filed about by name, same promotion_assertion_runs table inside a tenant schema the test just provisioned, same 42P01 :undefined_table, same {:error, {:transaction_failed, %Postgrex.Error{}}} wrapper. M1/M2 are four-axis matches to ISS-0109 failure 3 / ISS-0116's RollbackTest signature: 3F000 :invalid_schema_name via get_namespace_oid, {:error, {:migration_failed, %MatchError{...}}}, the assertion 'assert {:ok, _applied_versions} = TenantProvisioning.replay_migrations(tenant.id)', raised from each module's OWN hand-rolled provisioned_tenant/0 (engine_test.exs:87, reconstruction_test.exs:85) -- exactly the un-instrumented population ISS-0116 predicts. B1 is DELIBERATELY NOT ATTRIBUTED to the class: it shares the assertion and the full-suite-only character but returns {:error, {:event_type_seed_failed, :tenant_not_provisioned}} with NO Postgrex error at all -- per req022 design line 266 that is the tenant_schemas REGISTRATION ROW being absent, short-circuiting before any SQL, a sub-signature neither ISS-0109 nor ISS-0116 records. Reported as a new variant with the gap stated. WHY THE BRANCH DID NOT CAUSE B1/B2. REVIEWER's expired Step 3d proof is not inherited or restated; a narrower one was re-derived. The failure family is exclusively database-mediated, so the question is whether the branch's new compiled code touches that machinery. It does not: grep -nE 'Repo|Ecto|Postgrex|Sandbox|tenant|prefix:|SQL' returns ZERO matches over BOTH test/support/status_history.ex and test/docs/requirement_status_invariants_test.exs -- the latter is 'use ExUnit.Case, async: true', not DataCase. Both are pure filesystem/YAML readers. Reach is bounded too: grep -rln for StatusHistory over test/ and lib/ returns only the two new files and two markdown docs; NO pre-existing test module references them, including RoleRegistryTest and PromotionAssertionRerunTest. Zero lib/ .ex changed. The one non-zero channel is stated honestly rather than dismissed: 13 async:true tests add marginal load to a timing-sensitive suite. It is bounded -- branch async time was LOWER (6.0s/5.7s vs main's 6.6s/6.5s) and too_many_connections is 0 in all four logs -- but cannot be excluded absolutely from four runs. SYMMETRY, the strongest single argument: each side independently produced exactly TWO singleton extras, neither reproducing in that side's own second run, all four in the same tenant-provisioning family. Same count, same character, same family, both sides -- a shared environmental condition sampled twice per side, not a branch introducing something. INVARIANTS: 13/13 PASS in FULL-SUITE context in BOTH branch runs, which is stronger than Step 4b's isolated result. Established in two halves -- that they RAN (branch totals exceed main's by exactly 13 in the test column, impossible otherwise) and that they PASSED (grep for RequirementStatusInvariantsTest returns 0 across all four logs, and all 27 branch-side failure headers were read individually). The Step 4f A4 failure is GONE; the 4d/4e/4f amendment held. DB NORMALISATION was symmetric and the prior harness is endorsed: run.sh ran 'MIX_ENV=test mix ecto.drop --quiet' pre-START before every one of the four runs on both sides, normalising the orphaned iss060_tenant_schemas_guard_backup confound identically; no connection intervention was needed (0 saturation). LIMITS STATED IN THE REPORT: two runs per side is a small sample, so B1/B2/M1/M2 are each recorded as 'observed once, not reproduced in that side's second run' -- an observation, NOT a stable-or-flaky verdict; M1/M2 in particular are not called stable main failures on one observation each. This step generated no new evidence and could not, for example, run role_registry_test.exs in isolation to see whether B1 reproduces alone. The suite is RED on both sides for pre-existing reasons; this branch does not make it redder. CLEANUP: tmp-testrunner/ moved to scratch/testrunner-WF03-ISS0119-20260821/ (git-ignored) and the project-root dir removed; the letflow-mainbase worktree removed and confirmed absent from git worktree list, with sibling letflow-wt2 untouched. No test or source file modified, nothing under docs/status/ touched, orchestrator.log and ISS-0193.yaml left uncommitted, registry.json not written.

issues.description: NEW VARIANT of the ISS-0116 tenant-provisioning family, not recorded by ISS-0109 or ISS-0116, and potentially the most diagnostically useful observation here. Letflow.Identity.RoleRegistryTest 'list_roles/0 (acceptance criterion 1) returns [] (not an error) against an empty tenant_role table' (test/letflow/role_registry_test.exs:174) failed in branch1 at the SAME assertion the whole family fails at -- assert {:ok, _applied_versions} = TenantProvisioning.replay_migrations(tenant.id), from __ex_unit_setup_1 at :133 -- but with right: {:error, {:event_type_seed_failed, :tenant_not_provisioned}} and NO Postgrex error. Every ISS-0109/0116 signature on record is a raw 3F000 invalid_schema_name or 42P01 undefined_table. Per lib/letflow/design/req022-tenant-schema-provisioning.md:266, :tenant_not_provisioned is returned when the tenant_schemas REGISTRATION ROW is absent, short-circuiting before any SQL touches the tenant schema. That points at the REGISTRY ROW disappearing rather than the schema -- a materially different locus from what ISS-0116 has been searching, and it may narrow that search. NOT attributed to the class here and NOT filed by this step, per the handoff. Observed once in four runs; did not reproduce in branch2. NOT caused by this branch (role_registry_test.exs is absent from the branch diff and does not reference the new StatusHistory module).

ISS-0109/ISS-0116 3F000 signature reproduced in TWO FURTHER un-instrumented modules on MAIN, neither named in either issue record: Letflow.EngineTest 'create/2 (REQ-059 AC6) -- child pin inheritance and conflict recording ...' (engine_test.exs:1177, raised from its own provisioned_tenant/0 at :87) and Letflow.Engine.ReconstructionTest 'AC6 -- {:lock_contention, instance_id} is its own distinct error shape' (reconstruction_test.exs:640, from provisioned_tenant/0 at :85). Both four-axis match the class. Both occurred in the SAME run (main1) on adjacent connection ids 28579 and 28585 about 15s apart, consistent with one transient window hitting two consecutive modules rather than two defects. This extends ISS-0116's scope exactly as ISS-0116 predicted -- the condition is not specific to the modules ISS-0109 happened to name -- and adds both modules to the ISS-0112 Letflow.TenantFixture adoption list, since both still carry hand-rolled provisioned_tenant/0 helpers. Main-side only; reported, not acted on, per the handoff. One observation each, so NOT characterised as stable main failures.

Process observation for the run record: this step's briefing stated tmp-testrunner/main2.log was killed mid-run with no END and no result line and must be treated as unusable. The file on disk is complete (START 08:32:41Z, Finished in 530.2 seconds, Result: 1261/1274 passed, Failed: 13 tests, LETFLOW_CHECK_EXIT=1, END 08:41:34Z) -- the run finished after the observation that judged it dead was made. Recovering it turned a 2-branch-vs-1-main comparison into 2-vs-2 and materially strengthened the verdict. Worth a line in the run record as a reminder to re-check a process presumed dead before discarding its artefacts.

result.next_action: Proceed to WF-04 Step 1 (RELEASE-VALIDATOR). Its independent re-run carries MORE weight than usual for this run, because this step generated no evidence of its own -- it analysed a prior attempt's logs by user direction. ORCH to triage the three issues above: the B1 registration-row variant (MAJOR, may narrow ISS-0116's search from the schema to the tenant_schemas registry row), the two new un-instrumented modules extending ISS-0116/ISS-0112 adoption, and the main2 briefing discrepancy. No merge blocker was found by this step.
